recaps.1:
Week 1 of the Finance League is in the books, and if your portfolio looks anything like some of these fantasy rosters, you might want to schedule a meeting with HR. Leading the charge this week was **Champ**, who dropped a jaw-dropping **192.36 points** and absolutely demolished **Team t-hart** by a margin of **86.52 points** — a blowout so lopsided it should come with a trigger warning. T-hart's 105.84 was bad enough on its own, but getting boat-raced by nearly 90 points in Week 1 is the kind of thing that follows you to the water cooler. Meanwhile, **Lapointe12** quietly put up a very respectable **170.62** to take the second spot in the standings, suggesting they may actually know what they're doing, which is frankly suspicious.

On the other end of the spectrum, **casper05** limped out of the gate with a league-low **85.82 points**, which is less a fantasy football score and more a cry for help. Close behind in the "please explain your draft strategy" competition were **mcooney32** (94.16) and **hniehaus** (96.06), rounding out the bottom of the standings like a trio of red stocks on a bad earnings day. There's nowhere to go but up, gentlemen — unless there is, in which case, thoughts and prayers.

The week's most heartbreaking story belongs to **Schmiddy1**, who scored a perfectly respectable **119.32 points** and still lost, earning the unluckiest team honors. That's the fantasy football equivalent of acing a presentation and still getting passed over for the promotion. On the flip side, **mmcelvaney** somehow scraped together **120.66 points** — barely more than Schmiddy — and walked away with a win, claiming the luckiest team award and proving once again that it's better to be lucky than good. Don't let it go to your head, mmcelvaney.

The week's nail-biter goes to **jhuang24**, who edged out **Crashee and Co.** by just **21.32 points** in what passes for a close game around here. It wasn't exactly coming down to the wire, but in a week where the reigning **DefendingChampion** only managed to scrape into third place at 136.4, nothing is guaranteed. The league is young, the stakes are fake, and the trash talk is very much real — see everyone in Week 2.
recaps.2:
Week 2 of the Finance League is in the books, and if your portfolio looked anything like some of these lineups, you'd be getting a margin call right about now. Leading the charge this week was Schmiddy1, who dropped a monstrous 191.58 points — the highest score of the week — and somehow still sits at 1-1. That's right, Schmiddy put up nearly 200 points in back-to-back weeks for a combined 310.9, the most points in the league, and has exactly one win to show for it. That's the kind of ROI that would get you fired in an actual finance job. Meanwhile, jhuang24 squeaked out a 2.28-point nailbiter over mmcelvaney to go 2-0, proving that in fantasy football, as in life, you don't have to be the best — you just have to be luckier than the person across from you.

Speaking of luck, let's talk about mcooney32, who limped to victory this week with a cozy 104.18 points — good enough to win, apparently, and earn the dubious honor of Luckiest Team of the Week. Meanwhile, Team t-hart dropped 150.66 and lost anyway, making them the Unluckiest Team of the Week and the proud owners of a 0-2 record despite outscoring half the league. T-hart is essentially the person who does all the work on the group project and still gets a C. We see you. We feel bad. Not bad enough to do anything about it, but still.

The week's most brutal storyline came courtesy of casper05, who absolutely steamrolled Lapointe12 by a staggering 58.72 points. That's not a fantasy football matchup, that's a hostile takeover. Lapointe12 now sits at 1-1 and probably needs to have a serious conversation with their waiver wire. And then there's DefendingChampion, who posted a league-low 65.76 points this week — a number so low it's almost impressive in its own right. The defending champ is now 1-1 with just 202.16 points on the season, which is less a title defense and more a controlled demolition.

At the bottom of the standings, hniehaus remains winless at 0-2 with a paltry 162.86 points for the season, which is somehow even fewer points than the defending champion has managed while also losing. On the bright side, the only way to go from here is up — or, more likely, to the waiver wire in a panic at 11pm on a Tuesday. IR All Stars, however, looks quietly dangerous at 2-0 with 236.76 points, doing their damage without much fanfare. Keep an eye on them. The Finance League is young, the stakes are petty, and the group chat is about to get very uncomfortable. See you next week.
recaps.3:
Week 3 of the Finance League is in the books, and if your portfolio looks anything like some of these rosters, it might be time to call HR. Leading the charge this week was jhuang24, who hung a league-high 143.76 points on the scoreboard and is now sitting pretty at 3-0 with 417 points on the season. Meanwhile, IR All Stars somehow also went 3-0 despite scoring nearly 75 fewer points than Schmiddy1 on the year — a fact that Schmiddy1 fans are absolutely not okay with. The standings are a lesson in schedule luck, and we're only three weeks in.

Speaking of luck, let's talk about the DefendingChampion, who took home the Luckiest Team award after winning with a pedestrian 98.38 points. Ninety-eight points. In full PPR. The defending champ is out here winning with a score that wouldn't have cracked the top half of the league on most weeks, and yet somehow they're 2-1. To add insult to injury, they also handed Lapointe12 the blowout loss of the week by a margin of 34.76 points. Lapointe12 scored a league-low 63.62, which is the kind of number that makes you want to stare at the waiver wire until your eyes bleed. Sixty-three points, folks. That's not a fantasy score, that's a golf round.

The unluckiest team this week was mcooney32, who dropped to 1-2 despite putting up a very respectable 134.78 points — the second-highest score of the week. That's the kind of performance that wins eight out of twelve matchups in any given week, and mcooney32 just happened to draw the wrong one. Brutal. Meanwhile, the nail-biter of the week came down to IR All Stars edging out hniehaus by just 2.64 points, which is the fantasy equivalent of losing a client pitch because of a typo. hniehaus falls to 0-3 with 266 total points on the season, and at this rate, the only thing they'll be drafting is an explanation email.
recaps.4:
Week 4 is in the books, and the Finance League continues to separate the portfolio managers from the interns. Leading the charge are jhuang24 and IR All Stars, both sitting at a pristine 4-0, though it's worth noting that IR All Stars has done it with nearly 90 fewer points than jhuang24 — which is either a testament to clutch performance or a schedule so soft it should come with a pillow. Either way, DefendingChampion is lurking at 3-1 after handing Team t-hart a 28-point beatdown this week, which is the fantasy equivalent of a margin call. t-hart is now 1-3 and has more points than three teams above them in the standings, which means the universe is simply not rooting for them right now.

This week's high score belongs to mmcelvaney, who put up a jaw-dropping 153.18 points and somehow still sits at 2-2. That's the kind of performance that makes you question everything — your roster, your life choices, the league format itself. Meanwhile, Lapointe12 limped to the week's low score with a dismal 88.82 points, which in a full-PPR league is genuinely impressive in the worst possible way. At 1-3 with only 414 points on the season, Lapointe12 is currently the league's version of a bad Q3 earnings report — ugly, hard to explain, and concerning for everyone involved.

The week's cruelest storyline goes to Schmiddy1, who scored a very respectable 129.88 points and still lost, earning the unluckiest team award. That's a gut-punch of a loss, and at 2-2, Schmiddy1 is staring at a top-four standings position that should probably have an extra win in it. On the flip side, hniehaus squeaked by with just 113.98 points to grab a win, cementing their status as this week's luckiest team and continuing what has become a deeply undeserved 1-3 record — apparently the one win came against the right person at the right time. And finally, a moment of silence for casper05's opponent Crashee and Co., who lost by 18 points in what was billed as a nailbiter. In this league, apparently, 18 points is close. Standards are different here.
recaps.5:
Week 5 is in the books, and the Finance League continues to separate the portfolio managers from the interns. Leading the charge once again is the unstoppable **jhuang24**, who somehow keeps winning games while everyone else is busy losing theirs, sitting pretty at a perfect **5-0** with 715 points on the season. Nobody in this league has figured out how to beat them yet, and at this point it might be time to just start pricing in the loss when you're scheduled against them. Meanwhile, **IR All Stars** holds down second place at 4-1 — a fitting name for a team that's apparently built its strategy around hoping everyone else gets hurt.

The headline of the week belongs to **Crashee and Co.**, who finally remembered they were in a fantasy football league and went absolutely nuclear with a league-high **196.26 points**, dropping the defending champ like a bad stock. Poor **DefendingChampion** put up a genuinely respectable **152.04 points** — good enough to beat eight other teams this week — but had the misfortune of running into Crashee's historic explosion, losing by **44.22 points** in the week's biggest blowout. Defending Champion is your unluckiest team of the week, and honestly, sometimes the market is just irrational.

On the other end of the spectrum, the week's nailbiter came down to a stomach-churning **0.32 points**, with **Team t-hart** squeaking past **hniehaus** by the thinnest of margins — **93.54 to 93.22**. That's the kind of win that makes you feel nothing, and the kind of loss that makes you want to renegotiate your lease. Hniehaus also takes home the low score of the week with those 93.22 points, which, when you consider that t-hart barely beat you and *they're* considered lucky, really says something about how your week went. T-hart, meanwhile, earns luckiest team of the week, which is a trophy you probably don't want to display publicly.

Looking at the broader standings, the 2-3 bracket is absolutely *crowded* — **Schmiddy1, Crashee, t-hart, casper05, and Lapointe12** are all knotted up and jockeying for position like analysts fighting over the last conference room. **mcooney32** and **hniehaus** are both sitting at 1-4, and while the season isn't over, the window is firmly closing. Someone in this league is going to make a desperate trade soon — probably for a running back who gets hurt in warmups. We'll see who blinks first.
recaps.6:
Week 6 is in the books, and the Finance League continues to deliver the kind of volatility that would make even the most seasoned trader sweat. Leading the charge as always is jhuang24, who remains a perfect 6-0 with 828.64 points on the season — at this point it's less a fantasy team and more a hostile takeover. Meanwhile, Crashee and Co. put up the week's high score of 143.2 points, which is an impressive number that unfortunately did not translate into a top-four standing, because that's just the kind of market we're in right now.

Speaking of brutal inefficiency, let's talk about Champ, who scored a very respectable 125.9 points and still lost, earning the unluckiest team of the week honors. The culprit? A 1.42-point nailbiter loss to Schmiddy1, who apparently needed every last reception to survive. Champ, you put up a number that would have beaten nine other teams this week, and you got the one matchup that didn't care. That's not bad management — that's just the universe being unprofessional.

On the other end of the spectrum, DefendingChampion scraped together 100.84 points and somehow walked away with a win, taking home the luckiest team award. The defending champ living off vibes and weak schedules — sounds about right. Meanwhile, IR All Stars had zero interest in close games, absolutely steamrolling Team t-hart by a margin of 75.42 points in the week's biggest blowout. At 5-1, IR All Stars is clearly not here to make friends.

And then there's Team t-hart, bless their heart, who posted a league-low 60.52 points and got demolished in the process. Sitting at 2-4 with 657.46 total points on the season, t-hart is the kind of portfolio you quietly unload before the quarterly review. The good news is there are still eight weeks to turn it around. The bad news is that's also what people said about WeWork.
recaps.7:
Week 7 is in the books, and the Finance League delivered its usual cocktail of heartbreak, dumb luck, and one truly embarrassing afternoon. Let's start at the top: **Team t-hart** put up a league-high 142.38 points this week, which is great, except t-hart is sitting at 3-4 and apparently saving all the good weeks for when they're already on the wrong side of .500. Beautiful timing. Meanwhile, **mmcelvaney** scraped together a ghastly 80.92 for the week's low score — a number so bad it raises real questions about whether anyone on that roster is actually playing football this season or just collecting DNPs and bye weeks. At 3-4, mmcelvaney can't afford many more weekends like that.

The most lopsided affair of the week saw **Crashee and Co.** absolutely steamroll **IR All Stars** by 50.82 points, which is less a fantasy football game and more a crime scene. IR All Stars, to their credit, are still somehow 5-2 on the season, but that kind of beatdown has a way of haunting you. On the other end of the drama spectrum, **mcooney32** survived a nail-biter against **Schmiddy1**, winning by just 3.66 points. Schmiddy1 is now 3-4, which stings extra hard given they're sixth in points scored at 929.32 — one of the most talented bad-luck rosters in the league. mcooney32 improves to 2-5, so "winning" is doing some heavy lifting there.

The universe had some feelings this week about fairness, and those feelings were: absolutely not. **jhuang24** scored 117.62 points — a perfectly respectable number — and somehow took the loss, earning the unluckiest team of the week. Despite the heartbreak, jhuang24 remains atop the standings at 6-1, so sympathy is limited. On the flip side, **hniehaus** limped to 87.9 points and still walked away with a win, claiming the luckiest team honors. At 2-5 with 673.74 points on the season — dead last in scoring — hniehaus should probably light a candle for whoever they played and quietly move on.
recaps.8:
Week 8 is in the books, and the Finance League continues to separate the portfolio managers from the interns. Leading the charge as always is **jhuang24**, who put up a monstrous **150.76 points** — the high score of the week — and cruised to yet another win to move to a dominant **7-1**. At this point, jhuang24 isn't just winning the league, they're making the rest of us look like we drafted with our eyes closed. Meanwhile, at the other end of the spectrum, **casper05** limped to a gut-wrenching **82.64 points**, the week's low score, somehow managing to field a lineup that looked more like a injury report than a fantasy roster. At 2-6, the playoff picture isn't just dim for casper05 — someone should probably unplug it entirely.

The cruelest story of the week belongs to **mcooney32**, who put up a very respectable **121.68 points** and still lost, earning the unfortunate title of Unluckiest Team of the Week. That's the kind of performance that deserves a W, a pat on the back, and maybe a stiff drink — instead they got nothing but a sixth loss and an existential crisis. On the flip side, **IR All Stars** continued their miraculous run of good fortune, scraping together just **96.06 points** and somehow still walking away with a victory, making them the Luckiest Team of the Week and moving to a shocking **6-2**. Six and two. With 96 points. Someone check the schedule and make sure IR All Stars hasn't just been playing casper05 every week.

The most lopsided affair of the week was the blowout delivered by **DefendingChampion** over **Champ** by a margin of **33.42 points**. There's something poetic — and a little cruel — about a team called Champ getting thoroughly dismantled by the Defending Champion. The naming rights alone feel like they've been revoked. On the other end of the drama spectrum, **IR All Stars** (yes, them again, riding their golden horseshoe into yet another week) edged out **mmcelvaney** by just **5.36 points** in the nail-biter of the week. mmcelvaney, sitting at 3-5, had to watch those last few points trickle in knowing it still wasn't enough — truly the fantasy football equivalent of losing a deal on the last page of the term sheet.

As we hit the back half of the season, the picture is getting clearer: jhuang24 is in a league of their own, DefendingChampion and IR All Stars are legitimate threats at 6-2, and **Crashee and Co.** quietly sits at 5-3 with the second-most points in the league at 1,072 — a sleeping giant that nobody seems to be talking about. Meanwhile, **hniehaus** brings up the rear at 2-6 with a league-worst **793.12 points scored**, which at this point feels less like a fantasy team and more like a charitable donation to everyone else's playoff hopes. Seven weeks down, the stretch run begins — may your waiver wire be fruitful and your injury notifications be silent.
recaps.9:
Week 9 is in the books, and the Finance League continues to separate the wolves from the people who probably should have just done a keeper league so they'd have an excuse. Leading the charge this week was **Crashee and Co.**, who dropped a league-high **162.96 points** and continues to lurk menacingly at 6-3 with the most points scored in the entire league at 1,234.98 — more than **jhuang24**, who somehow leads the standings at 8-1 despite scoring fewer total points. jhuang24 is essentially the fantasy football equivalent of a guy who keeps getting promoted without anyone understanding why. Enjoy the first-place seat while it's warm.

The **DefendingChampion** had a strong week of their own, handing **Schmiddy1** the blowout of the week by a brutal margin of **71.7 points**. Schmiddy1's **85.18 points** was the lowest score in the league this week, which is impressive in the worst possible way. At 4-5, the wheels aren't exactly falling off the bus — it's more like the bus was towed and Schmiddy1 is standing in an empty parking lot holding their lineup card wondering what happened.

Spare a thought for **casper05**, who scored a respectable **105.68 points** this week and still walked away with the Unluckiest Team award, almost certainly because they had the misfortune of drawing a tough matchup on a week they finally showed up. At 2-7, casper05 is basically the fantasy equivalent of a person who gets to work on time for the first time all month and finds out there's a mandatory 7am meeting they weren't told about. Meanwhile, **mmcelvaney** coasted in with just **110.56 points** — the luckiest team of the week — and somehow squeaked past **Lapointe12** by just **14.8 points** in the week's closest game. mmcelvaney is 4-5 and surviving entirely on vibes and favorable scheduling at this point.

Playoff positioning is starting to get spicy. **IR All Stars** sits at 6-3 with under 1,000 points scored, meaning they are winning games through sheer force of luck or matchup manipulation — either way, the rest of the league should be nervous. **Champ** at 5-4 is right on the bubble, and the bottom of the standings — **mcooney32**, **Lapointe12**, **casper05**, and **hniehaus** — are all statistically still alive but probably shouldn't clear their playoff schedules just yet. We've got a few weeks left to find out who's been playing chess and who's been playing Candy Land.
